file_roles.evidence: Two guards are added at the reply site: '} else {' becomes '} else if (exchange.getOut(false) != null) {', and the send condition gains 'rce == null &&'. The commit message says 'Fixed a NPE'; these stop a reply being sent after an exception and stop a null out being dereferenced, which is error handling where the failure surfaced.

JMSReplyTo was copied onto the outgoing message unconditionally; the fix wraps it in 'if (exchange.getPattern().isOutCapable())' and otherwise logs 'Exchange is not out capable, Ignoring JMSReplyTo'. This file owns the header-mapping invariant that the reporter says was violated.

The not-out-capable branch now strips the inherited headers: 'exchange.getIn().setHeader("JMSReplyTo", null)' and the same for JMSCorrelationID, guarded by '!endpoint.isPreserveMessageQos() && !endpoint.isExplicitQosEnabled()'. The reporter named this file's process(Exchange) as 'the root of the bug'.

rationale: The reported symptom is a 20 second request timeout, 'The OUT message was not received within: 20000 millis on the exchange', which fires in the producer's request/reply wait, the same method the reporter identifies as the root. The report quotes no log line with a file or line, so the log site cannot be placed. Two files correct the JMSReplyTo handling itself; the consumer-side listener only gains guards against replying after an exception and against a null out.
notes: Five fix commits span months and the final patch does not change the 'if (exchange.getPattern().isOutCapable())' line the reporter pointed at; it strips the headers instead. The gold set is therefore the union of several rounds of fixing, which weakens single-commit attribution.
